title: Swe entry scenario code review global state
topic: Swe entry scenario code review global state
question: You're reviewing a teammate's pull request and notice a function uses a mutable default argument (or a shared module-level list) to accumulate results across calls. What would you flag, and why?
idealAnswer:
Identifies that a mutable default argument (or shared module-level state) persists across function calls instead of being fresh each time, since it's created once when the function is defined, not per call

Explains the concrete bug this causes: calling the function multiple times silently accumulates leftover data from previous calls instead of starting empty

Recommends the standard fix: default to None and create a new empty list/dict inside the function body when needed

Frames this as a review comment with a clear reason and suggested fix, not just 'this looks wrong', showing how they'd communicate it to the teammate

Bonus: notes this is a well-known gotcha in languages like Python where default argument values are evaluated once at function definition time
